svg.text: Our testbed · Bowling Green / Warren County, KY · status Nov 2026
Where the Bowling Green flood-mapping testbed stands
Phases 0–3 · every number is a real result from 2016–2025 Sentinel-1, OPERA, USGS and ESA data
Big idea:
The cut-off is solved. What remains is water the radar cannot see: under trees.
The question
Where does Bowling Green flood, how deep,
and on which days, in fine detail? Rivers
and karst sinkholes both flood here.
The ingredients

g.text: dates imaging the county; 0 = none yet

svg.text: Radar sees through cloud: Sentinel-1
since 2016, NISAR since Oct 2025. Two
gauges and news reports say when it
flooded.
Phase 0: high water under a
satellite?

g.text: river level at the moment of the pass:

svg.text: Floods here rise and fall fast. Only 16
of 574 passes caught a river at 16 ft or
more at the moment of the pass.
Phase 1: dark = water
Calm water looks dark. A cut-off taken
from the image alone fails in a county
with this little water; the gauge picks a
sensible one.
Phase 2: the cut-off is stable

g.text: each dot = one flood pass: its best cut-off
one shared cut-off costs only 0.02 in F1

svg.text: On 16 flood passes each pass's best
cut-off lies within −16.0 to −13.5 dB.
One cut-off (-15.25 dB) works for all of
them.
Phase 2: what radar still
misses
Half the expected flood is under trees,
and radar sees only 9% of it. In open
fields it sees 75–91%.
Phase 3: optical check

g.text: wooded floodplain the gauge says is wet:
leafless trees in Feb: optical sees through

svg.text: Floods bring clouds: 10 of 11 optical
scenes were covered. The clear one
confirms the gauge's expected area and
shows water under the leafless trees.
Status and next steps
Done: calendar, cut-off, open-field maps.
Open: water under trees (NISAR L-band, VH
tests) and daily maps between passes.
Data: NASA/ESA Sentinel-1 (OPERA RTC, DSWx-S1, DSWx-HLS), NASA-ISRO NISAR, USGS gauges and 3DEP, ASF HAND, JRC water, ESA WorldCover, Groundsource. Schematic illustration.
